from ext_tool.scanner import scan_local_extensions

docs.title: Classify extensions against Open VSX
docs.text:
import asyncio
from ext_tool.scanner import scan_local_extensions
from ext_tool.marketplace import classify_extensions

raw = scan_local_extensions()
registry = asyncio.run(classify_extensions(raw))

for ext in registry.extensions:
    print(f"{ext.id}  →  {ext.marketplace.value}")

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Install ext-tool via uv or pipx:

uv tool install ext-tool
# or
pipx install ext-tool

Then generate your extension registry from your currently-installed extensions:

ext generate

This scans your local VS Code / Cursor extensions directory, classifies each extension against the Open VSX registry, and writes a TOML registry to ~/.config/ext-tool/extensions.toml.

To install all extensions from an existing registry on a new machine:

ext install

@app.callback(invoke_without_command=True)
def main(
    ctx: typer.Context,
    *,
    version: Annotated[
        bool,
        typer.Option("--version", "-v", help="Show version and exit.", is_eager=True),
    ] = False,
    debug: Annotated[
        bool,
        typer.Option("--debug", help="Enable debug logging.", envvar="EXT_DEBUG"),
    ] = False,
    helper: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option(
            "--helper",
            help="VS Code-compatible CLI to use  [dim](default: cursor)[/]",
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
    extensions_file: Annotated[
        Path | None,
        typer.Option(
            "--extensions-file",
            help="Path to extensions.toml  [dim](default: ~/.config/ext-tool/extensions.toml)[/]",
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
) -> None:
    r"""[bold cyan]ext[/] — manage VS Code / Cursor extensions from a TOML registry.

    \b
    Configuration is stored in [dim]~/.config/ext-tool/[/]

    Run [bold]ext COMMAND --help[/] for command-specific options.
    """
    if version:
        console.print(f"[bold cyan]ext-tool[/] [green]{_pkg_version('ext-tool')}[/]")
        raise typer.Exit

    log_path = setup_logging(debug=debug)

    ensure_config_dir()
    cfg = AppConfig.load()
    if helper is not None:
        cfg.helper = helper
    if extensions_file is not None:
        cfg.extensions_file = extensions_file
    cfg.debug = debug

    ctx.ensure_object(dict)
    ctx.obj["config"] = cfg

    if debug and log_path:
        console.print(f"[dim]Debug log → [bold]{log_path}[/bold][/dim]")

class AppConfig(BaseSettings):
    """User-facing configuration for ext-tool.

    Loaded from (in order of precedence):
      1. CLI flags (injected by typer callback)
      2. Environment variables prefixed with EXT_
      3. ~/.config/ext-tool/config.toml
      4. Defaults below
    """

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="EXT_",
        env_file=".env",
        extra="ignore",
    )

    helper: Annotated[
        str,
        Field(default="cursor", description="VS Code-compatible CLI binary to use."),
    ] = "cursor"

    extensions_file: Annotated[
        Path,
        Field(default=EXTENSIONS_FILE, description="Path to extensions.toml registry."),
    ] = EXTENSIONS_FILE

    extensions_dir: Annotated[
        Path | None,
        Field(default=None, description="Override VS Code extensions directory."),
    ] = None

    concurrency: Annotated[
        int,
        Field(
            default=10, ge=1, le=_MAX_CONCURRENCY, description="Max concurrent Open VSX requests."
        ),
    ] = 10

    debug: Annotated[
        bool,
        Field(default=False, description="Enable debug logging."),
    ] = False

    @classmethod
    def load(cls) -> Self:
        """Load config from file + environment."""
        if CONFIG_FILE.exists():
            with CONFIG_FILE.open("rb") as config_fh:
                file_data = tomllib.load(config_fh)
        else:
            file_data = {}
        return cls(**file_data)

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Persist current config to ~/.config/ext-tool/config.toml."""
        ensure_config_dir()
        serialized = self.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"debug"})
        cleaned = {
            field_name: str(field_val) if isinstance(field_val, Path) else field_val
            for field_name, field_val in serialized.items()
            if field_val is not None
        }
        CONFIG_FILE.write_bytes(tomli_w.dumps(cleaned).encode())

The full extension registry — owns its own serialisation.

Source code in src/ext_tool/models.py 
class ExtensionRegistry(BaseModel):
    """The full extension registry — owns its own serialisation."""

    generated_at: datetime = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC),
    )
    extensions: list[Extension] = Field(default_factory=list)

    # ── Lookup helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def by_id(self, ext_id: str) -> Extension | None:
        """Return the extension with this id, or None."""
        normalized = ext_id.lower()
        return next((ext for ext in self.extensions if ext.id == normalized), None)

    def filter_marketplace(self, marketplace: Marketplace) -> list[Extension]:
        """Return only extensions matching the given marketplace."""
        return [ext for ext in self.extensions if ext.marketplace == marketplace]

    # ── TOML round-trip ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def to_toml(self) -> str:
        """Serialise registry to TOML string."""
        ts = self.generated_at.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        open_vsx = sum(1 for ext in self.extensions if ext.marketplace == Marketplace.OPEN_VSX)
        microsoft = len(self.extensions) - open_vsx
        open_vsx_label = "open-vsx"

        header = (
            "# VS Code / Cursor extension registry\n"
            f"# Generated: {ts}\n"
            f"# Total: {len(self.extensions)}"
            f"  ({open_vsx_label}: {open_vsx}, microsoft: {microsoft})\n"
            "#\n"
            "# marketplace values:\n"
            f'#   "{open_vsx_label}"  — installed via: $helper --install-extension <id>\n'
            '#   "microsoft" — installed via: VSIX download from gallery.vsassets.io\n'
            "\n"
        )
        payload = {"extension": [ext.model_dump(mode=_JSON_MODE) for ext in self.extensions]}
        return header + cast(str, tomli_w.dumps(payload))

    def save(self, path: Path) -> None:
        """Write registry to *path* as TOML."""
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(self.to_toml(), encoding=_UTF8)

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> Self:
        """Load registry from a TOML file."""
        with path.open("rb") as registry_fh:
            registry_data = tomllib.load(registry_fh)
        extensions = [Extension(**entry) for entry in registry_data.get("extension", [])]
        return cls(extensions=extensions)

    # ── Export ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def export(self, path: Path, fmt: ExportFormat) -> None:
        """Export registry to *path* in the requested format."""
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        match fmt:
            case ExportFormat.TOML:
                path.write_text(self.to_toml(), encoding=_UTF8)
            case ExportFormat.JSON:
                rows = [ext.model_dump(mode=_JSON_MODE) for ext in self.extensions]
                path.write_text(
                    json.dumps({"extensions": rows}, indent=2),
                    encoding=_UTF8,
                )
            case ExportFormat.CSV:
                _export_csv(self.extensions, path)

    # ── Merge ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def merge(self, other: "ExtensionRegistry") -> "ExtensionRegistry":
        """Return a new registry merging *other* into self (other wins on conflict)."""
        index = {ext.id: ext for ext in self.extensions}
        for ext in other.extensions:
            index[ext.id] = ext
        return ExtensionRegistry(
            generated_at=datetime.now(UTC),
            extensions=sorted(index.values(), key=lambda entry: (entry.marketplace, entry.id)),
        )

def load_from_export(
    path: Path,
    fmt: ExportFormat | None = None,
) -> ExtensionRegistry:
    """Load a registry from a previously exported file.

    If *fmt* is None the format is inferred from the file suffix.
    """
    if fmt is None:
        fmt = _infer_format(path)

    match fmt:
        case ExportFormat.TOML:
            return ExtensionRegistry.load(path)
        case ExportFormat.JSON:
            registry_data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding=_UTF8))
            extensions = [Extension(**entry) for entry in registry_data.get("extensions", [])]
            return ExtensionRegistry(extensions=extensions)
        case ExportFormat.CSV:
            return _load_csv_registry(path)

async def classify_extensions(
    raw_extensions: list[dict[str, str]],
    *,
    concurrency: int = 10,
) -> ExtensionRegistry:
    """Check every extension against Open VSX and return a populated registry.

    Args:
        raw_extensions: Output from :func:`ext_tool.scanner.scan_local_extensions`.
        concurrency:    Max simultaneous Open VSX HTTP requests.

    Returns:
        :class:`~ext_tool.models.ExtensionRegistry` with marketplace field set.
    """
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)
    cache = DiskCache(_OPEN_VSX_CACHE_FILE, ttl=_OPEN_VSX_CACHE_TTL)
    check_results = await _gather_checks(raw_extensions, sem, cache)
    cache.flush()

    extensions = [
        _build_extension(raw, on_open_vsx=bool(flag))
        for raw, flag in zip(raw_extensions, check_results, strict=False)
    ]
    extensions.sort(key=_sort_key)
    return ExtensionRegistry(extensions=extensions)

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
1. Read extensions.json for the deduplicated canonical ID list — VS Code's own source of truth, handles multiple versions on disk cleanly.
  2. For every extension (open-vsx and microsoft alike) read <relativeLocation>/package.json for displayName and description. This avoids any extra API calls for metadata — the data is already local.
  3. The Open VSX check (in marketplace.py) is performed separately and only to determine the marketplace routing field.

def resolve_extensions_dir(helper: str, override: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    """Return the extensions directory to scan.

    Args:
        helper:   The VS Code-compatible CLI binary name (e.g. ``"cursor"``).
        override: If provided, use this path directly.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When the resolved directory does not exist.
    """
    if override is None:
        path = _DEFAULT_DIRS.get(helper, Path.home() / ".vscode" / _EXTENSIONS_DIR)
    else:
        path = override

    if not path.exists():
        msg = f"Extensions directory not found: {path}"
        raise FileNotFoundError(msg)

    logger.debug("Extensions directory: %s", path)
    return path

def scan_local_extensions(extensions_dir: Path) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Return a list of raw extension dicts from the local filesystem.

    Each dict contains:
        id, version, relative_location, publisher, publisher_display_name,
        display_name, description

    The ``marketplace`` field is intentionally absent — it is assigned by
    :func:`ext_tool.marketplace.classify_extensions` after async Open VSX checks.

    Args:
        extensions_dir: Path to the VS Code extensions directory.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When ``extensions.json`` is missing.
    """
    index_file = extensions_dir / _EXTENSIONS_INDEX
    if not index_file.exists():
        msg = f"extensions.json not found in {extensions_dir}"
        raise FileNotFoundError(msg)

    raw: list[dict[str, Any]] = json.loads(index_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    logger.debug("extensions.json contains %d entries", len(raw))
    deduped = _deduplicate_entries(raw)
    logger.debug("Total unique extensions: %d", len(deduped))
    return [_entry_to_dict(extensions_dir, entry) for entry in deduped]

docs.title: DiskCache
docs.text:
A write-back TTL cache backed by a JSON file on disk.

Entries are held in memory and flushed to disk in a single write via :meth:flush. This avoids redundant I/O when many keys are written in one batch (e.g. one entry per extension in a asyncio.gather call).

Cache file format::

{ "<key>": { "v": <value>, "ts": <unix-timestamp-float> } }

    """A write-back TTL cache backed by a JSON file on disk.

    Entries are held in memory and flushed to disk in a single write via
    :meth:`flush`.  This avoids redundant I/O when many keys are written in
    one batch (e.g. one entry per extension in a ``asyncio.gather`` call).

    Cache file format::

        { "<key>": { "v": <value>, "ts": <unix-timestamp-float> } }
    """

    _path: Path
    _ttl: float
    _store: dict[str, tuple[Any, float]]

    def __init__(self, path: Path, ttl: float = DEFAULT_TTL) -> None:
        """Initialise the cache, loading any valid (non-stale) entries from disk."""
        self._path = path
        self._ttl = ttl
        self._store = {}
        self._load()

    # ── public ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def get(self, key: str) -> Any | None:
        """Return the cached value for *key*, or ``None`` if absent/stale."""
        entry = self._store.get(key)
        if entry is None:
            return None
        cached_val, ts = entry
        if time.time() - ts > self._ttl:
            self._store.pop(key, None)
            return None
        return cached_val

    def set(self, key: str, cached_val: Any) -> None:
        """Store *cached_val* in memory under *key* (no disk I/O)."""
        self._store[key] = (cached_val, time.time())

    def flush(self) -> None:
        """Write the current in-memory state to disk.

        Errors are logged and swallowed — a cache write failure must never
        prevent the surrounding command from completing.
        """
        try:
            self._write_cache()
        except Exception:
            logger.debug("Cache flush failed", exc_info=True)

    def _write_cache(self) -> None:
        """Serialize and write the in-memory store to disk."""
        self._path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        payload = {
            cache_key: {"v": cached_val, "ts": ts}
            for cache_key, (cached_val, ts) in self._store.items()
        }
        self._path.write_text(json.dumps(payload))
        logger.debug("Cache flushed to %s (%d entries)", self._path, len(payload))

    # ── private ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _load(self) -> None:
        """Load cache from disk and drop stale entries."""
        if not self._path.exists():
            return
        try:
            raw: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = json.loads(self._path.read_text())
        except Exception:
            logger.debug("Cache load failed, starting empty", exc_info=True)
            self._store = {}
        else:
            now = time.time()
            for cache_key, entry in raw.items():
                ts = float(entry["ts"])
                if now - ts <= self._ttl:
                    self._store[cache_key] = (entry["v"], ts)

docs.title: ext generate
docs.text:
Scan the local extensions directory, classify each extension via Open VSX, and write the registry to ~/.config/ext-tool/extensions.toml.

ext generate
ext generate --dry-run   # print what would be written without saving

docs.title: ext install
docs.text:
Install all (or filtered) extensions from the registry.

ext install                        # install all
ext install --marketplace open-vsx # only Open VSX extensions
ext install --marketplace microsoft # only Microsoft extensions
ext install --dry-run               # print what would be installed

docs.title: ext update
docs.text:
Shortcut for running ext generate followed by ext install.

ext update

docs.title: ext export
docs.text:
Export the registry to a file.

ext export registry.toml
ext export registry.json --format json
ext export registry.csv  --format csv

docs.title: ext import
docs.text:
Import extensions from an export file.

ext import registry.toml

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All configuration lives in ~/.config/ext-tool/config.toml and can also be set via environment variables prefixed with EXT_.

Key Default Description helper cursor VS Code-compatible CLI binary extensions_file ~/.config/ext-tool/extensions.toml Registry path concurrency 10 Max concurrent Open VSX requests debug false Enable debug logging
